title: Specific features of communicative interaction between a psychologist and a virtual client in psychotherapeutic speech skills training
abstract: Context and relevance. The quality of psychotherapeutic speech is a key predictor of therapeutic effectiveness and the strength of the therapeutic alliance. The development of AI simulator for training psychotherapists requires evaluating their ecological validity. The study is theoretically based on models of therapeutic discourse analysis. Objective. To describe the specific characteristics of verbal interaction between a psychologist and an AI simulator and to identify the limitations of such interaction. A secondary goal is to propose a methodology or a set of metrics for evaluating this interaction. Hypothesis. The text of the training sessions will exhibit all structural and thematic features inherent in psychotherapeutic sessions in general. Methods and materials. The study involved 10 practicing psychologists (8 female, age M = 35, SD = 2). The corpus consisted of 16 text dialogues with a standardized synthetic client, “Anna”. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and content analysis with coding of speech acts according to the Verbal Response Modes (VRM) taxonomy. The frequency of intervention types was recorded. Results. The most frequent speech acts were “Directive instruction” (48,9%) and “Exploratory question” (23,7%). A significant portion consisted of alliance-building interventions, particularly “Validation and empathy” (16,9%). However, speech acts related to client resistance were completely absent (0%). Conclusions. The significance of the “zone of proximal development” concept for training psychotherapists is highlighted. The dialogue in a simulated environment was confirmed to be authentic but functionally limited. It corresponds to real practice in technical execution but lacks relational skills due to the “ideal”, compliant behavior of the synthetic client. Future AI trainers should include non-compliant behavior scenarios.
